components.note: 氵 (water, 三点水) — marks water and liquids, as in 海 sea, 河 river, 汤 soup; 沾 is getting wet or touching, as in 沾边.
占 (zhàn) — close sound: 沾 zhān. 占 also sounds out 站 zhàn and 粘 zhān.

example.hanzi: 他的手上沾了一点油。
example.pinyin: Tā de shǒu shàng zhān le yìdiǎn yóu.
example.english: He got a bit of oil on his hand.
example.fact: 沾 describes getting a bit of something on you: 沾上 (to get stained). It also has figurative uses: 沾光 means to benefit from someone else's good fortune, and 沾边 means 'to be related to'.

examples.hanzi: 你的衣服上沾了灰。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ de yīfu shang zhān le huī.
examples.english: Your clothes have gotten dusty.

examples.hanzi: 他沾了朋友的光,免费进去了。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhān le péngyou de guāng, miǎnfèi jìnqù le.
examples.english: He benefited from his friend and got in free.

components.note: 衤 (clothing, 衣字旁) — clothes: 衬 shirt, 衫, 裙 skirt, 被 quilt; 裤 is trousers.
库 (kù) sounds exactly like 裤.

example.hanzi: 这条裤子太长了。
example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo kùzi tài cháng le.
example.english: These trousers are too long.
example.fact: 裤 is nearly always 裤子, and its measure word is 条 (一条裤子), because pants are viewed as long strips. 牛仔裤 (jeans) and 短裤 (shorts) are common, and 裤脚 is the hem of the trouser leg.

examples.hanzi: 他穿着一条牛仔裤。
examples.pinyin: Tā chuān zhe yì tiáo niúzǎikù.
examples.english: He is wearing a pair of jeans.

examples.hanzi: 我想买一条短裤。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng mǎi yì tiáo duǎnkù.
examples.english: I want to buy a pair of shorts.

components.note: 礻 (altar, spirit — form of 示) — rites and blessings: 神, 礼, 祝, 祈; 福 is good fortune from the gods.
畐 (fú) sounds exactly like 福; also in 幅 fú, 副 fù, 富 fù.

example.hanzi: 祝你新年幸福平安，福气满满。
example.pinyin: Zhù nǐ xīnnián xìngfú píng'ān, fúqi mǎnmǎn.
example.english: Wishing you happiness and peace in the new year, full of good fortune.
example.fact: At Chinese New Year 福 is pasted on doors, often upside down: 倒 (dào, 'upside down') sounds like 到 (dào, 'arrive'), so a 倒福 means 'fortune has arrived'. 福气 means 'good luck' or 'blessing'.

examples.hanzi: 春节时家家户户贴福字。
examples.pinyin: Chūnjié shí jiājiā hùhù tiē fú zì.
examples.english: At Spring Festival every household puts up the character "fu".

examples.hanzi: 你真有福气!
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhēn yǒu fúqi!
examples.english: You're really blessed!

components.note: 日 (sun) — marks light and time, as in 明, 晴, 早; 晓 is dawn, when the sun comes up, and so to know.
尧 (yáo) is a loose hint for xiǎo; 烧 shāo and 浇 jiāo share it.
彳 (step) — walking and going, as in 行, 往, 很 very.
寸 (hand) — oldest form is a hand grabbing a cowrie shell (money): 得 is "to obtain". The shell has worn down to 旦.

example.hanzi: 我早就晓得他会来。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zǎo jiù xiǎode tā huì lái.
example.english: I already knew he would come.
example.fact: The 'tip-of-the-tongue' phenomenon, where a person is certain they know a word but cannot recall it, has been documented in nearly every language studied. Researchers attribute it to a temporary breakdown in retrieving a word's sound even though its meaning remains fully accessible.

examples.hanzi: 你晓得去火车站怎么走吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiǎode qù huǒchēzhàn zěnme zǒu ma?
examples.english: Do you know how to get to the train station?

examples.hanzi: 我不晓得他今天为什么没来。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bù xiǎode tā jīntiān wèishénme méi lái.
examples.english: I don't know why he didn't come today.

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过, 进, 送; 迟 is slow going, late.
尺 (chǐ) is a close sound match, tone differs.
日 (sun) — time and day, as in 时, 晚, 明: the sun at the top of a sprout, early morning. 早 also gives 草 cǎo and 澡 zǎo.

example.hanzi: 谎言迟早会被揭穿。
example.pinyin: Huǎngyán chízǎo huì bèi jiēchuān.
example.english: Lies will be exposed sooner or later.
example.fact: Tectonic plates drift at roughly the same speed fingernails grow, just a few centimeters a year. Yet given enough time this slow creep has torn apart supercontinents like Pangaea and, geologists predict, will eventually reassemble today's continents into a new one, sometimes called Pangaea Ultima, in around 250 million years.

examples.hanzi: 你迟早要面对这个问题。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ chízǎo yào miànduì zhège wèntí.
examples.english: Sooner or later you will have to face this problem.

examples.hanzi: 只要努力学习，迟早会有收获的。
examples.pinyin: Zhǐyào nǔlì xuéxí, chízǎo huì yǒu shōuhuò de.
examples.english: As long as you study hard, you'll get results sooner or later.

components.note: 电 (electric) — simplified from 電: 雨 rain over 申, a lightning bolt (申 originally pictured a flash).
台 (tái) as a sound part appears in 抬 tái, 胎 tāi, 苔 tái, and also in 治 zhì and 始 shǐ.

example.hanzi: 这家电台每天播放新闻和音乐节目。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàntái měitiān bòfàng xīnwén hé yīnyuè jiémù.
example.english: This radio station broadcasts news and music programs every day.
example.fact: On October 30, 1938, Orson Welles's radio dramatization of The War of the Worlds, staged as a series of fake news bulletins about a Martian invasion, reportedly caused real alarm among some listeners who tuned in after the introduction explaining it was fiction.

examples.hanzi: 我爸爸喜欢在车里听电台。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bàba xǐhuan zài chē lǐ tīng diàntái.
examples.english: My dad likes listening to the radio in the car.

examples.hanzi: 她在一家电台做主持人。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài yì jiā diàntái zuò zhǔchírén.
examples.english: She works as a host at a radio station.

meanings: (idiom) powerless to do anything about it

components.note: 無 (traditional) — began as a person dancing with ornaments (same root as 舞). 'None' is a borrowed sense; 无 is an old variant of 無 and the shape does not explain it.
能 (can) — originally a picture of a bear, a strong animal (熊 xióng adds fire 灬); "strong, able" gave "can".
力 (strength) — visible inside 为. Memory aid: putting strength 力 into doing something; 为 is 'to do, to act' and, in 因为, 为什么, 'because/for'.
為 (traditional) — often explained as a hand leading an elephant to work. 为 is a cursive simplification, so the picture is no longer visible.
力 (strength) — an old picture of an arm or a plough, a tool of effort. As a radical it marks strength: 办, 助, 动, 努, 男.

example.hanzi: 面对突如其来的自然灾害，人类有时也无能为力。
example.pinyin: Miànduì tūrúqílái de zìrán zāihài, rénlèi yǒushí yě wúnéngwéilì.
example.english: Faced with sudden natural disasters, humans are sometimes powerless to do anything.
example.fact: The 2011 Tōhoku earthquake off Japan's coast was powerful enough to shift the Earth's axis by an estimated 17 centimeters and shorten the length of a day by about 1.8 microseconds — a reminder of how even the largest engineered defenses can be overwhelmed by geophysical forces of that scale.

examples.hanzi: 这件事我真的无能为力，对不起。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì wǒ zhēn de wúnéngwéilì, duìbuqǐ.
examples.english: I really can't do anything about this, sorry.

examples.hanzi: 看着朋友难过，我却无能为力。
examples.pinyin: Kànzhe péngyou nánguò, wǒ què wúnéngwéilì.
examples.english: I watched my friend feel sad but was powerless to help.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — 刂 is 刀 (knife) as in 到, 别, 利; punishing was once done by cutting.
讠 (speech) — 讠 (言, words) — 罚 originally also meant scolding.

example.hanzi: 他因为迟到被罚了一百元。
example.pinyin: Tā yīnwèi chídào bèi fá le yìbǎi yuán.
example.english: He was fined a hundred yuan for being late.
example.fact: 罚 means to punish and in daily life most often 'to fine': 罚款 (fine), 罚站 (make someone stand as punishment) and 处罚. 罚 is also in the pair 赏罚, 'reward and punishment'.

examples.hanzi: 开车超速会被罚款。
examples.pinyin: Kāichē chāosù huì bèi fákuǎn.
examples.english: You'll be fined for speeding.

examples.hanzi: 老师罚我们站了十分钟。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī fá wǒmen zhàn le shí fēnzhōng.
examples.english: The teacher made us stand for ten minutes as punishment.

components.note: 旅 (travel) — a flag with people gathered under it: a troop on the march, then travellers on a journey.

example.hanzi: 我们计划一次长途旅行。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen jìhuà yí cì chángtú lǚxíng.
example.english: We are planning a long trip.
example.fact: 旅 once denoted a military unit of five hundred soldiers, which is why 旅 can still translate as 'brigade'. It later widened to a group on the move: 旅行 (travel), 旅游 (tourism), 旅馆 (hotel) and 旅客 (traveler).

examples.hanzi: 我喜欢旅游,尤其是去海边。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan lǚyóu, yóuqí shì qù hǎibiān.
examples.english: I like traveling, especially to the seaside.

examples.hanzi: 旅馆就在车站对面。
examples.pinyin: Lǚguǎn jiù zài chēzhàn duìmiàn.
examples.english: The hotel is right across from the station.

components.note: 厂 (shelter) — 厂 stands for a building or shelter, as here — 厨 is the room where food is cooked, in 厨房 kitchen and 厨师 chef.

example.hanzi: 妈妈在厨房做饭。
example.pinyin: Māma zài chúfáng zuòfàn.
example.english: Mom is cooking in the kitchen.
example.fact: 厨 is a bound form found in 厨房 (kitchen), 厨师 (chef) and 下厨 ('to go into the kitchen', i.e. to cook). 厨 is the simplified form of 廚.

examples.hanzi: 他的梦想是当一名厨师。
examples.pinyin: Tā de mèngxiǎng shì dāng yì míng chúshī.
examples.english: His dream is to become a chef.

examples.hanzi: 妈妈的厨艺很好。
examples.pinyin: Māma de chúyì hěn hǎo.
examples.english: Mom's cooking skill is great.

components.note: 土 (earth) — a green shoot pushing up from the ground: growth, birth, life. 生 also sounds out 性 xìng, 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.
氵 (water) — marks water, as in 河, 海, 湖; 涯 is the water's edge, hence a limit, as in 生涯 career.
厓 (yá) gives the sound exactly: 涯 yá, also in 崖 yá.

example.hanzi: 他的职业生涯长达三十多年。
example.pinyin: Tā de zhíyè shēngyá cháng dá sānshí duō nián.
example.english: His career spanned more than thirty years.
example.fact: Jazz singer Tony Bennett performed publicly for more than 70 years, releasing an album, Love for Sale, with Lady Gaga in 2021 at age 95 while already living with Alzheimer's disease — one of the longest continuously active careers in modern popular music.

examples.hanzi: 她的教师生涯从一所乡村小学开始。
examples.pinyin: Tā de jiàoshī shēngyá cóng yì suǒ xiāngcūn xiǎoxué kāishǐ.
examples.english: Her teaching career began at a village primary school.

examples.hanzi: 这位运动员宣布结束自己的运动生涯。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi yùndòngyuán xuānbù jiéshù zìjǐ de yùndòng shēngyá.
examples.english: This athlete announced the end of his sporting career.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: guarding with the hands.
户 (hù, door) gives the exact sound; 户 means door or household.
灬 (fire) — fire and heat, as in 热 hot, 点 dot, 黑 black: light shining.
昭 (zhāo) is a close sound clue for zhào; 昭 itself means bright.

example.hanzi: 出国旅行之前，请检查你的护照是否过期。
example.pinyin: Chūguó lǚxíng zhīqián, qǐng jiǎnchá nǐ de hùzhào shìfǒu guòqí.
example.english: Before traveling abroad, please check whether your passport has expired.
example.fact: The modern passport format traces to a 1920 League of Nations conference in Paris, which standardized the small booklet design, photograph requirement, and page dimensions still used by most countries today.

examples.hanzi: 办护照需要带两张照片。
examples.pinyin: Bàn hùzhào xūyào dài liǎng zhāng zhàopiàn.
examples.english: You need to bring two photos to apply for a passport.

examples.hanzi: 我的护照放在行李箱里了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de hùzhào fàng zài xínglixiāng lǐ le.
examples.english: My passport is in the suitcase.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — knowing is something you can say aloud; 口 sits in many speech words (问 ask, 告 tell).
矢 (shǐ, arrow) is only a loose sound clue today; the same 知 sound is in 智 zhì (wisdom).
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; knowing means being able to name.
只 (zhǐ) is a loose sound clue for shí; the part replaces 戠 in the traditional 識.

example.hanzi: 阅读是获取知识的重要途径。
example.pinyin: Yuèdú shì huòqǔ zhīshi de zhòngyào tújìng.
example.english: Reading is an important way to gain knowledge.
example.fact: The ancient Library of Alexandria, founded in Egypt around the 3rd century BC, is estimated to have held several hundred thousand papyrus scrolls and employed scholars tasked with copying and translating every book that passed through the city's port. Its eventual loss is still cited as one of history's greatest blows to accumulated human knowledge.

examples.hanzi: 他的历史知识非常丰富。
examples.pinyin: Tā de lìshǐ zhīshi fēicháng fēngfù.
examples.english: His knowledge of history is very rich.

examples.hanzi: 多读书可以增长知识。
examples.pinyin: Duō dúshū kěyǐ zēngzhǎng zhīshi.
examples.english: Reading more can increase your knowledge.

components.note: 廾 (two hands) — in 開 two hands lift the bar of a gate; 开 is the simplified shape. Compare 关 (close).
会 (meet, can) — simplified from 會, a lid on a container: bringing things together; hence meeting, then "can" (huì).

example.hanzi: 明天上午我们要开会讨论新项目。
example.pinyin: Míngtiān shàngwǔ wǒmen yào kāihuì tǎolùn xīn xiàngmù.
example.english: Tomorrow morning we're going to have a meeting to discuss the new project.
example.fact: A widely cited internal study at Amazon found meetings with more than eight attendees became significantly less effective, leading founder Jeff Bezos to popularize the 'two pizza rule': if two pizzas can't feed the group, the meeting has too many people.

examples.hanzi: 经理正在会议室开会。
examples.pinyin: Jīnglǐ zhèngzài huìyìshì kāihuì.
examples.english: The manager is having a meeting in the conference room.

examples.hanzi: 今天下午三点开会，别迟到。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān xiàwǔ sān diǎn kāihuì, bié chídào.
examples.english: The meeting is at three this afternoon, so don't be late.

components.note: 又 (hand) — a hand holding a branch 十: to prop up, support; 支 also sounds out 枝 zhī branch and 肢 zhī limb.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 付 is handing 寸 something to a person.
付 (fù) is also the sound in 附 fù, 府 fǔ, 符 fú and 腐 fǔ.

example.hanzi: 你可以用信用卡支付账单。
example.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ yòng xìnyòngkǎ zhīfù zhàngdān.
example.english: You can pay the bill with a credit card.
example.fact: The earliest known use of paper money dates to China's Tang and Song dynasties, around the 7th to 11th centuries, when merchants began issuing promissory notes called 'jiaozi' to avoid carrying heavy strings of copper coins over long trade routes.

examples.hanzi: 这家店可以用手机支付。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn kěyǐ yòng shǒujī zhīfù.
examples.english: You can pay with your phone at this shop.

examples.hanzi: 公司每个月十号支付工资。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī měi gè yuè shí hào zhīfù gōngzī.
examples.english: The company pays salaries on the tenth of every month.

components.note: 页 (head) — 页 is the head, as in 题, 顶, 颜; 领 is the neck and then to lead.
令 (lìng) — near sound — 领 is lǐng; 令 also sounds out 龄 líng and 铃 líng.
衤 (clothing) — marks garments, as in 衬, 衫, 裤; 袖 is a sleeve.
由 (yóu) hints at the sound: 袖 xiù is close to 抽 chōu and 油 yóu, which share it.

example.hanzi: 他被大家推选为团队的领袖。
example.pinyin: Tā bèi dàjiā tuīxuǎn wéi tuánduì de lǐngxiù.
example.english: He was elected by everyone as the team's leader.
example.fact: Antarctic explorer Ernest Shackleton is often studied as a model of crisis leadership: after his ship Endurance was crushed by ice in 1915, he led all 28 crew members to survival over nearly two years, including an 800-mile open-boat journey across the Southern Ocean, without losing a single man.

examples.hanzi: 他从小就有领袖的气质。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóngxiǎo jiù yǒu lǐngxiù de qìzhì.
examples.english: He has had the qualities of a leader since childhood.

examples.hanzi: 这位领袖受到了人们的尊敬。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi lǐngxiù shòudào le rénmen de zūnjìng.
examples.english: This leader earned the respect of the people.

components.note: 小 (small) — three small dots, tiny grains. As a radical it appears in 少 few, 尖 sharp.
亻 (person) — marks people and their actions, as in 你, 做, 住; 偷 is a person stealing.
俞 (yú) is a loose hint for tōu; 愉 yú and 输 shū share it.

example.hanzi: 昨晚有个小偷闯入了邻居家。
example.pinyin: Zuówǎn yǒu gè xiǎotōu chuǎngrù le línjū jiā.
example.english: A thief broke into the neighbor's house last night.
example.fact: The Mona Lisa's fame skyrocketed after it was stolen from the Louvre in 1911 by an Italian handyman who believed it should be returned to Italy. The painting was missing for over two years, and the theft generated more publicity than the artwork had received in the preceding four centuries.

examples.hanzi: 在地铁上要小心小偷。
examples.pinyin: Zài dìtiě shàng yào xiǎoxīn xiǎotōu.
examples.english: Watch out for thieves on the subway.

examples.hanzi: 警察抓到了那个偷钱包的小偷。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá zhuādào le nàge tōu qiánbāo de xiǎotōu.
examples.english: The police caught the thief who stole the wallet.

components.note: 见 (see) — seeing and vision: 看, 现, 视, 览; 观 is to watch. 又 only stands in for the old sound part 雚 (guàn).
手 (hand) — over 目 (eye): a hand shading the eyes to look into the distance. 目 marks seeing words, as in 眼, 睡.

example.hanzi: 全家人一起观看了世界杯决赛。
example.pinyin: Quán jiā rén yīqǐ guānkànle shìjièbēi juésài.
example.english: The whole family watched the World Cup final together.
example.fact: The 1969 Apollo 11 moon landing broadcast is estimated to have been watched live by roughly 600 million people worldwide — about a fifth of the planet's population at the time — making it one of the largest simultaneous shared television events in human history.

examples.hanzi: 欢迎大家来现场观看比赛。
examples.pinyin: Huānyíng dàjiā lái xiànchǎng guānkàn bǐsài.
examples.english: Everyone is welcome to come and watch the match live.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们安静地观看了整场演出。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen ānjìng de guānkàn le zhěng chǎng yǎnchū.
examples.english: The children watched the whole performance quietly.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 拉, 推; 挣 is to struggle, also to earn (zhèng).
争 (zhēng) gives the sound exactly: 挣 zhēng, also in 睁 zhēng.
扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 拉, 提; 扎 is to bind or prick with the hand.

example.hanzi: 溺水的人在水中拼命挣扎。
example.pinyin: Nìshuǐ de rén zài shuǐzhōng pīnmìng zhēngzhá.
example.english: The drowning person struggled desperately in the water.
example.fact: Real drowning rarely looks like the dramatic splashing shown in movies. Lifeguards are trained to recognize the 'instinctive drowning response,' in which a person's arms press down involuntarily at their sides and the head tilts back, making genuine drowning often silent and easy for bystanders to miss.

examples.hanzi: 小鸟在网里挣扎着想飞出去。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo niǎo zài wǎng lǐ zhēngzházhe xiǎng fēi chūqù.
examples.english: The little bird struggled in the net, trying to fly out.

examples.hanzi: 他在是否辞职的问题上很挣扎。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài shìfǒu cízhí de wèntí shàng hěn zhēngzhá.
examples.english: He is torn over whether or not to quit his job.

components.note: 王 (jade, 玉 with its dot dropped) — jewels and polished things: 玩, 现, 理, 玻; 球 first meant a round gem.
求 (qiú) sounds exactly like 球.
贝 (cowry shell, money) — wealth and trade: 财, 费, 买, 货; 员 was a paid member or staff. 员 also sounds out 圆 yuán.

example.hanzi: 这位球员在比赛中打进了两个球。
example.pinyin: Zhè wèi qiúyuán zài bǐsài zhōng dǎ jìn le liǎng gè qiú.
example.english: This player scored two goals in the match.
example.fact: Brazilian footballer Pelé is officially credited by the Guinness Book of Records with 1,279 career goals across professional matches, a tally that includes friendlies and exhibition games, though goals scored in fully competitive matches alone number closer to 767.

examples.hanzi: 这支球队有很多年轻的球员。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhī qiúduì yǒu hěn duō niánqīng de qiúyuán.
examples.english: This team has many young players.

examples.hanzi: 球员们正在场上热身。
examples.pinyin: Qiúyuánmen zhèngzài chǎng shàng rèshēn.
examples.english: The players are warming up on the field.

meanings: inch (unit of length equal to 2.54 cm.)

components.note: 艹 (grass, plants) — plants and flowers: 花, 草, 茶; 英 first meant a flower, then outstanding, then hero.
央 (yāng) is a loose sound hint (-ng); also in 映 yìng and 殃 yāng.
寸 (inch) — a hand with a dot marking the pulse about an inch from the wrist; as a part it appears in 对, 寻, 守, 村.

example.hanzi: 这台电视的屏幕有五十五英寸。
example.pinyin: Zhè tái diànshì de píngmù yǒu wǔshíwǔ yīngcùn.
example.english: This television has a 55-inch screen.
example.fact: The inch was historically defined in a 1324 English statute as the length of three barleycorns laid end to end. It wasn't standardized to its precise modern value of exactly 2.54 centimeters until an international agreement among English-speaking countries in 1959.

examples.hanzi: 我想买一台三十二英寸的显示器。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng mǎi yì tái sānshí'èr yīngcùn de xiǎnshìqì.
examples.english: I want to buy a 32-inch monitor.

examples.hanzi: 一英寸大约等于两点五四厘米。
examples.pinyin: Yì yīngcùn dàyuē děngyú liǎng diǎn wǔ sì límǐ.
examples.english: One inch is roughly equal to 2.54 centimeters.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 拉, 提; 推 is to push.
隹 (zhuī) is a loose hint for tuī; 堆 duī and 谁 shéi share it.
艹 (plants) — marks grass and plants, as in 花, 草, 菜; 荐 first meant a grass fed to animals, later to offer or recommend.

example.hanzi: 医生推荐我每天多喝水。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng tuījiàn wǒ měitiān duō hē shuǐ.
example.english: The doctor recommended that I drink more water every day.
example.fact: Netflix's recommendation engine is estimated to influence over 80% of the content its subscribers watch. The company famously ran a $1 million open competition, the Netflix Prize, from 2006 to 2009 to find an algorithm that could improve its movie-rating predictions by just 10%.

examples.hanzi: 你能给我推荐一本好看的小说吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng gěi wǒ tuījiàn yì běn hǎokàn de xiǎoshuō ma?
examples.english: Can you recommend a good novel to me?

examples.hanzi: 老师推荐他去参加这个比赛。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī tuījiàn tā qù cānjiā zhège bǐsài.
examples.english: The teacher recommended him for this competition.

components.note: 丁 (dīng) — a nail seen from above; as a part it sounds out 钉 dīng, 订 dìng, 顶 dǐng, 灯 dēng.

example.hanzi: 请把土豆切成丁。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ tǔdòu qiē chéng dīng.
example.english: Please dice the potatoes.
example.fact: 丁 is the fourth in the ten Heavenly Stems (甲乙丙丁), so it is used like 'D' in a ranking. In cooking it means diced pieces (肉丁, 土豆丁), and it is also a common surname.

examples.hanzi: 他叫小丁,是我的同事。
examples.pinyin: Tā jiào Xiǎo Dīng, shì wǒ de tóngshì.
examples.english: He's called Xiao Ding, and he's my colleague.

examples.hanzi: 这道菜里有鸡丁和花生。
examples.pinyin: Zhè dào cài li yǒu jīdīng hé huāshēng.
examples.english: This dish has diced chicken and peanuts.

components.note: 马 (horse) — marks horses and riding, as in 骑 ride, 骂 scold, 驾 drive; 骚 is to stir up or annoy, as in 骚扰.
蚤 (zǎo, flea) hints at the sound: 骚 sāo is close to 搔 sāo (scratch).
扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 推; 扰 is to stir up and disturb.
尤 (yóu) is only a loose sound hint for rǎo.

example.hanzi: 她报警投诉遭到陌生人骚扰。
example.pinyin: Tā bàojǐng tóusù zāodào mòshēngrén sāorǎo.
example.english: She called the police to report being harassed by a stranger.
example.fact: The term 'sexual harassment' as a legal concept was coined in 1975 by a group of women at Cornell University organizing around a colleague's experience, and it entered U.S. federal case law within a decade, reshaping workplace policy worldwide.

examples.hanzi: 我每天都接到骚扰电话。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ měi tiān dōu jiēdào sāorǎo diànhuà.
examples.english: I get nuisance calls every day.

examples.hanzi: 蚊子整晚骚扰我，我根本睡不着。
examples.pinyin: Wénzi zhěng wǎn sāorǎo wǒ, wǒ gēnběn shuì bù zháo.
examples.english: Mosquitoes pestered me all night and I couldn't sleep at all.

meanings: to take in and care for

components.note: 攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 改, 放: to gather by force or hand.
丩 (jiū) is only a loose sound clue for shōu.
羊 (yáng) hints at the sound: 养 yǎng is close, as in 样 yàng and 洋 yáng; the old form 養 added 食 food.

example.hanzi: 这对夫妇决定收养一个孤儿。
example.pinyin: Zhè duì fūfù juédìng shōuyǎng yī gè gū'ér.
example.english: This couple decided to adopt an orphan.
example.fact: Cross-species adoption happens in the wild more often than once assumed. Researchers have documented capuchin monkeys raising an orphaned marmoset and lionesses in Kenya nursing orphaned oryx calves, behavior scientists attribute to strong hormonal caregiving instincts overriding typical species boundaries.

examples.hanzi: 他们收养了一只被丢弃的小狗。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen shōuyǎng le yì zhī bèi diūqì de xiǎo gǒu.
examples.english: They took in an abandoned puppy.

examples.hanzi: 她从小被一户好心人家收养。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóngxiǎo bèi yí hù hǎoxīn rénjiā shōuyǎng.
examples.english: She was adopted as a child by a kind family.

components.note: 弓 (bow) — the vertical stroke 丨 is the string being drawn back on a bow — 引 is to pull, then to attract and to cite.
火 (fire) — fire and heat: 灯, 烧, 炸, 热; 爆 is to burst in flames.
暴 (bào) sounds exactly like 爆, and means violent.

example.hanzi: 拆弹专家小心地引爆了那枚炸弹。
example.pinyin: Chāidàn zhuānjiā xiǎoxīn de yǐnbàole nà méi zhàdàn.
example.english: The bomb disposal expert carefully detonated the bomb.
example.fact: Modern controlled demolition of skyscrapers relies on precisely timed explosive charges, sometimes delayed by mere milliseconds between floors, so that a building collapses almost straight downward into its own footprint rather than toppling outward into surrounding structures.

examples.hanzi: 工人们在山上引爆了炸药，开出一条路。
examples.pinyin: Gōngrénmen zài shān shàng yǐnbào le zhàyào, kāi chū yì tiáo lù.
examples.english: Workers detonated explosives on the mountain to open up a road.

examples.hanzi: 这条新闻引爆了网络上的讨论。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo xīnwén yǐnbào le wǎngluò shàng de tǎolùn.
examples.english: This news set off a storm of discussion online.

components.note: 艹 stands in for 竹 (bamboo) in the traditional 節, bamboo joints: sections, then festivals and knots.
日 (sun, day) — a picture of the sun, once round with a dot, now squared off. As a radical it marks light and time: 明, 晴, 时.

example.hanzi: 春节是中国最重要的传统节日。
example.pinyin: Chūnjié shì Zhōngguó zuì zhòngyào de chuántǒng jiérì.
example.english: Spring Festival is China's most important traditional holiday.
example.fact: The Spring Festival travel rush in China, known as chunyun, is considered the largest annual human migration on Earth, with an estimated three billion trips made across roughly 40 days as people travel home for the Lunar New Year.

examples.hanzi: 节日的时候，街上到处都挂着灯笼。
examples.pinyin: Jiérì de shíhou, jiē shàng dàochù dōu guàzhe dēnglong.
examples.english: During the festival, lanterns hang everywhere on the streets.

examples.hanzi: 你最喜欢哪个节日？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zuì xǐhuan nǎge jiérì?
examples.english: Which holiday do you like best?

components.note: 隹 (zhuī, short-tailed bird) — 难 was first the name of a bird; "hard" is a borrowed use. The 又 here stands in for the traditional left part.
土 (earth) — marks ground and soil, as in 地, 城, 墙; 堪 is to bear or withstand.
甚 (shèn) is a loose hint for kān; 勘 kān shares it.

example.hanzi: 他的失言让在场所有人都感到难堪。
example.pinyin: Tā de shīyán ràng zàichǎng suǒyǒu rén dōu gǎndào nánkān.
example.english: His slip of the tongue made everyone present feel embarrassed.
example.fact: Humans are the only animal known to blush, a reflex Charles Darwin called 'the most peculiar and most human of all expressions.' It's triggered by adrenaline widening the blood vessels in the face and is difficult or impossible to suppress voluntarily.

examples.hanzi: 被老师当众批评，他觉得很难堪。
examples.pinyin: Bèi lǎoshī dāngzhòng pīpíng, tā juéde hěn nánkān.
examples.english: Being criticized by the teacher in public made him feel embarrassed.

examples.hanzi: 她的问题让我一时很难堪。
examples.pinyin: Tā de wèntí ràng wǒ yìshí hěn nánkān.
examples.english: Her question put me in an awkward spot for a moment.

components.note: 石 (stone) — marks stone and hard things, as in 破, 码, 砖; 硬 is hard.
更 (gēng) is only a loose sound hint for yìng.
巾 (cloth) — marks cloth and silk, as in 布, 带, 帽; silk was early money, hence 币 currency.

example.hanzi: 他把口袋里的硬币都倒在了桌子上。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ kǒudài lǐ de yìngbì dōu dào zài le zhuōzi shàng.
example.english: He poured all the coins out of his pocket onto the table.
example.fact: The earliest known coins were minted in the kingdom of Lydia, in present-day Turkey, around 600 BC, made from a naturally occurring gold-silver alloy called electrum and stamped with a lion's head to guarantee their weight and value.

examples.hanzi: 我们用一枚硬币来决定谁先走。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yòng yì méi yìngbì lái juédìng shéi xiān zǒu.
examples.english: We used a coin toss to decide who goes first.

examples.hanzi: 这台自动售货机只收硬币。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tái zìdòng shòuhuòjī zhǐ shōu yìngbì.
examples.english: This vending machine only accepts coins.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢: giving permission is spoken.
午 (wǔ) is only a loose sound clue for xǔ.
口 (mouth) — speech or assent: to say "OK". 可 is also a famous sound part: 河 hé, 歌 gē, 哥 gē, 何 hé all take their sound from it.

example.hanzi: 没有经过许可，任何人不得进入这个区域。
example.pinyin: Méiyǒu jīngguò xǔkě, rènhé rén bùdé jìnrù zhège qūyù.
example.english: No one may enter this area without permission.
example.fact: The world's oldest known patent system dates to 1474 in the Republic of Venice, which granted inventors a ten-year exclusive right to their creations, an early legal framework that influenced the patent systems most countries still use today.

examples.hanzi: 开餐馆需要先申请营业许可。
examples.pinyin: Kāi cānguǎn xūyào xiān shēnqǐng yíngyè xǔkě.
examples.english: To open a restaurant you first need to apply for a business license.

examples.hanzi: 如果天气许可，我们明天去爬山。
examples.pinyin: Rúguǒ tiānqì xǔkě, wǒmen míngtiān qù páshān.
examples.english: If the weather permits, we'll go hiking tomorrow.

components.note: 成 (chéng) is a sound clue for 城 chéng, 诚 chéng and 盛 chéng: the same sound.
年 (year) — first drawn as a person carrying harvested grain: one harvest per year. Seen in 今年, 去年, 年轻.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 这部电影只适合成年人观看。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng zhǐ shìhé chéngniánrén guānkàn.
example.english: This movie is only suitable for adults to watch.
example.fact: Neuroscientists have found that the human prefrontal cortex, responsible for impulse control and long-term planning, doesn't finish developing until around age 25 — well after most legal definitions of adulthood, which helps explain why risk-taking behavior tends to peak in the late teens and early twenties.

examples.hanzi: 成年人要对自己的行为负责。
examples.pinyin: Chéngniánrén yào duì zìjǐ de xíngwéi fùzé.
examples.english: Adults must take responsibility for their own actions.

examples.hanzi: 门票成年人五十元，儿童免费。
examples.pinyin: Ménpiào chéngniánrén wǔshí yuán, értóng miǎnfèi.
examples.english: Tickets are fifty yuan for adults and free for children.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 海; 深 is deep water.
罙 (shēn) — same sound — 深 is shēn; 罙 also sounds out 探 tàn.
口 (mouth) — breath and speech: 吸, 叫, 喊; 呼 is to breathe out or call.
乎 (hū) sounds exactly like 呼.
口 (mouth) — breath and speech: 呼, 吃, 喝; 吸 is to breathe in.
及 (jí) is a loose sound hint for xī; same part in 级 jí and 极 jí.

example.hanzi: 感到紧张的时候，试着深呼吸几次。
example.pinyin: Gǎndào jǐnzhāng de shíhou, shìzhe shēnhūxī jǐ cì.
example.english: When you feel nervous, try taking a few deep breaths.
example.fact: Slow, deep breathing activates the vagus nerve, which signals the parasympathetic nervous system to lower heart rate and blood pressure. This is the physiological basis for why deliberate deep breathing is one of the fastest, most reliable ways to calm the body during acute stress.

examples.hanzi: 上台之前，她先深呼吸了一下。
examples.pinyin: Shàng tái zhīqián, tā xiān shēnhūxī le yíxià.
examples.english: Before going on stage, she took a deep breath first.

examples.hanzi: 医生让我放松，慢慢地深呼吸。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng ràng wǒ fàngsōng, mànmàn de shēnhūxī.
examples.english: The doctor told me to relax and breathe deeply and slowly.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — marks the mouth and lips, as in 吃, 喝, 吹; 吻 is a kiss.
勿 (wù) is a loose hint for wěn; 物 wù shares the part.
合 (join) — a lid fitting over an opening 口: things that fit together. 合 also appears in 答 dá, 给 gěi and 拾 shí.

example.hanzi: 他的指纹与现场发现的完全吻合。
example.pinyin: Tā de zhǐwén yǔ xiànchǎng fāxiàn de wánquán wěnhé.
example.english: His fingerprints completely matched the ones found at the scene.
example.fact: Even identical twins, who share the same DNA, have different fingerprints. Ridge patterns are shaped partly by random pressure and position variations in the womb rather than genetics alone, making fingerprints one of the few truly unique physical identifiers between twins.

examples.hanzi: 他的说法和事实不吻合。
examples.pinyin: Tā de shuōfǎ hé shìshí bù wěnhé.
examples.english: His account doesn't match the facts.

examples.hanzi: 这两份报告的数据完全吻合。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liǎng fèn bàogào de shùjù wánquán wěnhé.
examples.english: The data in these two reports match perfectly.

components.note: 衤 (clothing) — marks clothes, as in 衬, 衫, 裤; 裸 is to be unclothed.
果 (guǒ) hints at the sound: 裸 luǒ is close, as in 课 kè and 颗 kē.

example.hanzi: 他赤裸着上身在海边跑步。
example.pinyin: Tā chìluǒ zhe shàngshēn zài hǎibiān pǎobù.
example.english: He ran along the beach with his upper body bare.
example.fact: 裸 means 'bare', as in 裸露 and 裸眼 (naked eye, unaided vision). Modern Chinese has coined terms like 裸婚 ('naked wedding') for marrying without a house, car or ring.

examples.hanzi: 这棵树的根裸露在地面上。
examples.pinyin: Zhè kē shù de gēn luǒlù zài dìmiàn shang.
examples.english: The tree's roots are exposed above the ground.

examples.hanzi: 星星用裸眼就能看见。
examples.pinyin: Xīngxing yòng luǒyǎn jiù néng kànjiàn.
examples.english: You can see the stars with the naked eye.

meanings: to collect information and report back

components.note: 氵 (water) — marks water, as in 河, 海, 湖; 汇 is waters flowing together.
匚 (box) — the container the water gathers in, as in 区.
扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; here a hand seizing someone to pass judgment.
卩 (kneeling person) — with 又 hand: sentencing a kneeling prisoner, then answering back: repay, report.

example.hanzi: 每周一，各部门经理都要向总裁汇报工作进度。
example.pinyin: Měi zhōuyī, gè bùmén jīnglǐ dōu yào xiàng zǒngcái huìbào gōngzuò jìndù.
example.english: Every Monday, department managers report their work progress to the president.
example.fact: During NASA's Apollo missions, flight controllers in Houston's Mission Control were organized so each specialist reported status only through a strict radio-call hierarchy — a communication discipline credited with helping the Apollo 13 team methodically diagnose and fix a life-threatening oxygen tank explosion in real time.

examples.hanzi: 小李明天要向领导汇报项目的情况。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo Lǐ míngtiān yào xiàng lǐngdǎo huìbào xiàngmù de qíngkuàng.
examples.english: Xiao Li will report on the project's status to the leadership tomorrow.

examples.hanzi: 有问题请及时向我汇报。
examples.pinyin: Yǒu wèntí qǐng jíshí xiàng wǒ huìbào.
examples.english: If there are any problems, please report them to me promptly.

components.note: 去 (to go) — 丢 looks like 去 with an extra stroke on top. Memory aid: something that 'goes' away is lost.
厶 (private, small) — the lower part, as in 去. The dictionary story (a lost piece of jade 玉) is a later reading, not proven.
月 (flesh) — ⺼ is the body radical (月 in 脑 brain, 脚 foot); 脸 is a body part, the face.
佥 (qiān) — loose hint — 脸 is liǎn; 佥 also sounds out 检 jiǎn, 险 xiǎn and 验 yàn, all ending in -ǎn.

example.hanzi: 他在众人面前摔倒，觉得很丢脸。
example.pinyin: Tā zài zhòngrén miànqián shuāidǎo, juéde hěn diūliǎn.
example.english: He fell in front of everyone and felt very embarrassed.
example.fact: Sociologist Erving Goffman's influential 1955 concept of 'face-work' argued that maintaining social dignity in front of others is a near-universal human concern, and cross-cultural studies have since found that fear of public embarrassment measurably affects decision-making in situations as varied as negotiating and public speaking.

examples.hanzi: 考试作弊真是太丢脸了。
examples.pinyin: Kǎoshì zuòbì zhēn shì tài diūliǎn le.
examples.english: Cheating on an exam is really shameful.

examples.hanzi: 别怕丢脸，大胆地说出来吧。
examples.pinyin: Bié pà diūliǎn, dàdǎn de shuō chūlái ba.
examples.english: Don't be afraid of losing face; just say it boldly.

components.note: 隹 (zhuī, short-tailed bird) — 难 was first the name of a bird; "hard" is a borrowed use. The 又 here stands in for the traditional left part.
又 (hand) — two hands pass a vessel: one gives, one receives; 授 shòu adds 扌 for "give".

example.hanzi: 他吃了不新鲜的食物，肚子很难受。
example.pinyin: Tā chī le bù xīnxiān de shíwù, dùzi hěn nánshòu.
example.english: He ate food that wasn't fresh and his stomach feels terrible.
example.fact: Symptoms of food poisoning can appear anywhere from thirty minutes to several weeks after eating contaminated food, depending on the pathogen: Staphylococcus aureus toxins can cause illness within an hour, while Listeria can take up to 70 days to produce symptoms.

examples.hanzi: 我感冒了，头疼得很难受。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gǎnmào le, tóu téng de hěn nánshòu.
examples.english: I have a cold, and my headache is making me feel awful.

examples.hanzi: 听到这个坏消息，大家心里都很难受。
examples.pinyin: Tīngdào zhège huài xiāoxi, dàjiā xīnlǐ dōu hěn nánshòu.
examples.english: Everyone felt sad when they heard this bad news.

components.note: 攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 收, 改: to drive away, set free.
方 (fāng) is a close sound clue for fàng; 方 also in 房 fáng and 访 fǎng.
尸 (body, rump) — body-related words: 尿 urine, 屎 dung, 尾 tail, 屋 room; here the buttocks and what comes out.
比 (bǐ) is only a loose sound hint for pì.

example.hanzi: 他说的都是放屁，别相信他。
example.pinyin: Tā shuō de dōu shì fàngpì, bié xiāngxìn tā.
example.english: What he said is nonsense, don't believe him.
example.fact: The average adult produces about half a liter to two liters of intestinal gas per day, mostly from bacteria in the colon fermenting undigested carbohydrates. Beans are a notorious culprit because they contain raffinose, a sugar humans lack the enzyme to break down before it reaches gut bacteria.

examples.hanzi: 电梯里有人放屁，大家都很尴尬。
examples.pinyin: Diàntī lǐ yǒu rén fàngpì, dàjiā dōu hěn gāngà.
examples.english: Someone farted in the elevator and everyone was embarrassed.

examples.hanzi: 他居然说我偷懒，简直是放屁！
examples.pinyin: Tā jūrán shuō wǒ tōulǎn, jiǎnzhí shì fàngpì!
examples.english: He actually said I'm lazy; that's total nonsense!

components.note: 壴 (drum) — a picture of a drum on a stand; 鼓 adds a hand with a stick 支 beating it.
手 (hand) — 手 as in 拿, 打, 拳; 掌 is the palm of the hand, then to control.
尚 (shàng) — near sound — 掌 is zhǎng; 尚 also sounds out 常 cháng, 堂 táng and 赏 shǎng.

example.hanzi: 演讲结束后，观众们热烈鼓掌。
example.pinyin: Yǎnjiǎng jiéshù hòu, guānzhòngmen rèliè gǔzhǎng.
example.english: After the speech ended, the audience applauded warmly.
example.fact: Researchers studying crowd acoustics have found that applause naturally synchronizes into rhythmic clapping within about 10-20 seconds when an audience wants to signal enthusiasm, then breaks back into random, faster clapping when the goal shifts to simply making the most total noise.

examples.hanzi: 大家一起为获奖的同学鼓掌。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā yìqǐ wèi huòjiǎng de tóngxué gǔzhǎng.
examples.english: Everyone clapped together for the classmate who won the prize.

examples.hanzi: 他刚唱完，台下就响起了鼓掌声。
examples.pinyin: Tā gāng chàng wán, tái xià jiù xiǎngqǐ le gǔzhǎng shēng.
examples.english: As soon as he finished singing, applause rang out from the audience.

components.note: 旅 (travel) — a flag with people gathered under it: a troop on the march, then travellers on a journey.
禾 (grain) — grain radical — 程 first meant to measure grain, hence standard, then course and journey; also in 种, 秋, 稿.
呈 (chéng) — same sound — 程 is chéng; 呈 also sounds out 逞 chěng.

example.hanzi: 这次穿越沙漠的旅程非常艰难。
example.pinyin: Zhè cì chuānyuè shāmò de lǚchéng fēicháng jiānnán.
example.english: This journey across the desert was extremely difficult.
example.fact: The Trans-Siberian Railway, spanning roughly 9,289 kilometers between Moscow and Vladivostok, is the longest single railway line in the world, crossing eight time zones and taking about a week to travel end to end.

examples.hanzi: 祝你旅程愉快！
examples.pinyin: Zhù nǐ lǚchéng yúkuài!
examples.english: Have a pleasant trip!

examples.hanzi: 这段旅程让我学到了很多东西。
examples.pinyin: Zhè duàn lǚchéng ràng wǒ xué dào le hěn duō dōngxi.
examples.english: This journey taught me a lot.

components.note: 将 (jiāng) is the trimmed top part: 奖 jiǎng sounds like 桨 jiǎng and 浆 jiāng.
今 (jīn) — the top part hints the sound — 金 is jīn, like 今; 金 means gold and metal.
金 (metal) — as a radical it shrinks to 钅 in simplified characters — 钱 money, 铁 iron, 钟 clock, 银 silver.

example.hanzi: 因为业绩出色，他今年拿到了一笔可观的奖金。
example.pinyin: Yīnwèi yèjì chūsè, tā jīnnián nádào le yī bǐ kěguān de jiǎngjīn.
example.english: Because of his outstanding performance, he received a substantial bonus this year.
example.fact: The Nobel Prize's cash award, funded from the estate of dynamite inventor Alfred Nobel, has fluctuated with the endowment's investment returns over more than a century. In 2023 the prize amount per category was 11 million Swedish kronor, worth just over $1 million USD, split among winners when a category has multiple laureates.

examples.hanzi: 年底公司会发一笔奖金。
examples.pinyin: Niándǐ gōngsī huì fā yì bǐ jiǎngjīn.
examples.english: The company will hand out a bonus at the end of the year.

examples.hanzi: 这次比赛的第一名可以拿到一万元奖金。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì bǐsài de dì-yī míng kěyǐ ná dào yí wàn yuán jiǎngjīn.
examples.english: The winner of this contest gets a ten thousand yuan prize.

components.note: 灬 (fire) — 灬 is fire at the bottom, as in 点, 照, 熟; 热 is heat.
犭 (animal) — marks animals, as in 猫 cat, 猪 pig, 猴 monkey; 狗 is a dog.
句 (jù) is a loose hint for gǒu; 够 gòu and 钩 gōu share it.

example.hanzi: 他午饭只吃了一根热狗。
example.pinyin: Tā wǔfàn zhǐ chīle yī gēn règǒu.
example.english: He only ate a hot dog for lunch.
example.fact: The hot dog's name may come from German immigrant vendors in 19th-century America who sold sausages from carts nicknamed "dog wagons," since sausage meat was jokingly rumored to contain dog meat. A popular but unverified story credits a 1901 New York cartoonist with popularizing the term because he couldn't spell "dachshund."

examples.hanzi: 棒球比赛的时候，我喜欢吃热狗。
examples.pinyin: Bàngqiú bǐsài de shíhou, wǒ xǐhuan chī règǒu.
examples.english: I like eating hot dogs during baseball games.

examples.hanzi: 请给我两个热狗，多加点番茄酱。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng gěi wǒ liǎng gè règǒu, duō jiā diǎn fānqiéjiàng.
examples.english: Two hot dogs please, with extra ketchup.

components.note: 马 (horse) — a galloping horse. As a radical it marks horses: 骑 ride, 驾 drive. It gives sound to 妈 mā, 吗 ma, 骂 mà and 码 mǎ.
丁 (dīng) — a nail seen from above; as a part it sounds out 钉 dīng, 订 dìng, 顶 dǐng, 灯 dēng.

example.hanzi: 马丁在会议上提出了一个新方案。
example.pinyin: Mǎdīng zài huìyì shàng tíchūle yī gè xīn fāng'àn.
example.english: Martin proposed a new plan at the meeting.
example.fact: Martin is the root of the word "martinet," a strict disciplinarian, named after Jean Martinet, a 17th-century French drill instructor whose rigid training methods became legendary in the army of Louis XIV. The word entered English within decades of his death in 1672.

examples.hanzi: 马丁是我们公司新来的工程师。
examples.pinyin: Mǎdīng shì wǒmen gōngsī xīn lái de gōngchéngshī.
examples.english: Martin is the new engineer at our company.

examples.hanzi: 你认识马丁吗？他是我大学同学。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ rènshi Mǎdīng ma? Tā shì wǒ dàxué tóngxué.
examples.english: Do you know Martin? He was my college classmate.

components.note: 片 (slice) — the right half of 木 split down the middle: a flat piece. See 版 bǎn (printing plate) and 牌 pái (card).
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 这部片子讲的是一个探险家的故事。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù piānzi jiǎng de shì yī gè tànxiǎnjiā de gùshì.
example.english: This film tells the story of an explorer.
example.fact: Early film reels were made of nitrate stock so flammable that projectionists worked in fireproof booths, since the material could ignite from the heat of the projector lamp alone and, once burning, released its own oxygen and kept burning even underwater. Studios didn't fully switch to safer acetate "safety film" until the 1950s.

examples.hanzi: 周末我们去租几部好看的片子吧。
examples.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen qù zū jǐ bù hǎokàn de piānzi ba.
examples.english: Let's rent a few good movies this weekend.

examples.hanzi: 医生看了看我的片子，说没有大问题。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng kàn le kàn wǒ de piānzi, shuō méiyǒu dà wèntí.
examples.english: The doctor looked at my scan and said there was no big problem.

components.note: 木 (tree) — a stroke added at the top of a tree marks its tip: the end. Compare 未 wèi with the longer lower stroke.
日 (sun, day) — a picture of the sun, once round with a dot, now squared off. As a radical it marks light and time: 明, 晴, 时.

example.hanzi: 这部电影描绘了世界末日的景象。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng miáohuìle shìjiè mòrì de jǐngxiàng.
example.english: This movie depicts a vision of the world's doomsday.
example.fact: The Doomsday Clock, maintained by the Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists since 1947, is a symbolic countdown to global catastrophe measured in minutes and seconds to midnight. In January 2023 the clock was moved to 90 seconds to midnight, its closest setting ever, citing the war in Ukraine and nuclear risk.

examples.hanzi: 他总以为世界末日就要来了。
examples.pinyin: Tā zǒng yǐwéi shìjiè mòrì jiù yào lái le.
examples.english: He always thinks the end of the world is coming.

examples.hanzi: 这家老店的末日终于到了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā lǎo diàn de mòrì zhōngyú dào le.
examples.english: The final days of this old shop have finally come.

components.note: 米 (rice, grain) — marks grain and food, as in 粉, 粮, 饭; 糖 is sugar, once made from grain.
唐 (táng) gives the sound exactly: 糖 táng, also in 塘 táng.
木 (tree) — trees and wood, as in 树 tree, 林 woods, 桌 table; the fruit hangs on the tree.
田 (field) here is the round fruit drawn on the tree. 果 also gives the sound for 课 kè and 颗 kē.

example.hanzi: 孩子们喜欢在万圣节收集糖果。
example.pinyin: Háizimen xǐhuan zài Wànshèngjié shōují tángguǒ.
example.english: Children love collecting candy on Halloween.
example.fact: The world's oldest known candy, found in an Egyptian tomb, was made from honey mixed with fruits and nuts, since refined sugar did not reach the Mediterranean world until centuries later. Sugarcane itself was first domesticated in New Guinea around 8,000 years ago before spreading to India and beyond.

examples.hanzi: 别吃太多糖果，对牙齿不好。
examples.pinyin: Bié chī tài duō tángguǒ, duì yáchǐ bù hǎo.
examples.english: Don't eat too much candy; it's bad for your teeth.

examples.hanzi: 奶奶的口袋里总是装着糖果。
examples.pinyin: Nǎinai de kǒudai lǐ zǒngshì zhuāngzhe tángguǒ.
examples.english: Grandma's pocket is always full of candy.

components.note: 目 (eye) — an eye turned on its side. As a radical it marks sight: 看 look, 眼 eye, 睡 sleep, 盯 stare.
凵 (open box) — the bottom part and dictionary radical. 击 simplifies 擊, whose 手 (hand) hinted at striking. Memory aid: a blow landing in a hollow.
者 (zhě) is a sound clue for 都 dū, 著 zhù, 煮 zhǔ, 猪 zhū and 诸 zhū; as a word it means "one who", as in 作者 author.

example.hanzi: 警方正在寻找案件的目击者。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng zhèngzài xúnzhǎo ànjiàn de mùjīzhě.
example.english: The police are looking for witnesses to the case.
example.fact: Cognitive psychologists have repeatedly shown that eyewitness memory is far less reliable than juries tend to assume, since stress, the presence of a weapon, and even the wording of a later question can distort a memory after the fact. DNA-exoneration studies of wrongful convictions in the United States found mistaken eyewitness identification was a contributing factor in a majority of the cases reviewed.

examples.hanzi: 目击者说他看见一辆白色的车逃走了。
examples.pinyin: Mùjīzhě shuō tā kànjiàn yí liàng báisè de chē táozǒu le.
examples.english: The eyewitness said he saw a white car drive away.

examples.hanzi: 这起事故没有找到任何目击者。
examples.pinyin: Zhè qǐ shìgù méiyǒu zhǎodào rènhé mùjīzhě.
examples.english: No witnesses were found for this accident.

components.note: 土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 场 field, 城 city, 坐 sit.
也 (yě) is a loose sound clue for dì; 也 also sounds out 他 tā and 池 chí.
面 (face) — a picture of a face; extended to the surface or side of things, as in 外面 outside.

example.hanzi: 雨后地面变得又湿又滑。
example.pinyin: Yǔ hòu dìmiàn biàn de yòu shī yòu huá.
example.english: After the rain, the ground became wet and slippery.
example.fact: Earth's land surface makes up only about 29% of the planet, with the rest covered by ocean, yet nearly all of human agriculture and infrastructure depends on that thin sliver of ground. Antarctica's ice sheet alone, if it melted, would raise global sea level by roughly 58 meters.

examples.hanzi: 地面太滑了，走路要小心。
examples.pinyin: Dìmiàn tài huá le, zǒulù yào xiǎoxīn.
examples.english: The floor is too slippery, so walk carefully.

examples.hanzi: 飞机慢慢降落到地面上。
examples.pinyin: Fēijī mànmàn jiàngluò dào dìmiàn shàng.
examples.english: The plane slowly landed on the ground.

meanings: also pr. [dai1 hui3 r5] or [dai1 hui5 r5]

components.note: 彳 (step, left foot) — walking and roads: 行, 往, 很, 得; 待 is to go toward and wait on someone.
寺 (sì) is only a loose sound clue; its family varies: 诗 shī, 持 chí, 特 tè, 等 děng.
会 (meet, can) — simplified from 會, a lid on a container: bringing things together; hence meeting, then "can" (huì).
儿 (child, legs) — shows a person's legs; in 兒 the top was a child's soft skull. As an ending (这儿) it adds the er sound; 儿 also in 先, 兄, 光.

example.hanzi: 你先坐一下,我待会儿就回来。
example.pinyin: Nǐ xiān zuò yīxià, wǒ dāihuìr jiù huílái.
example.english: Sit down for a moment; I'll be back shortly.
example.fact: The perception that time passes differently under stress or boredom is well documented: psychologists have found that people asked to estimate elapsed time during a frightening event, such as a fall, consistently overestimate the duration afterward, even though their real-time judgment during the event is accurate. This gap is attributed to how densely the brain encodes memories during high-adrenaline moments.

examples.hanzi: 我现在有点忙，待会儿给你回电话。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiànzài yǒudiǎn máng, dāihuìr gěi nǐ huí diànhuà.
examples.english: I'm a bit busy now; I'll call you back later.

examples.hanzi: 待会儿一起去吃午饭，好吗？
examples.pinyin: Dāihuìr yìqǐ qù chī wǔfàn, hǎo ma?
examples.english: Shall we go have lunch together in a bit?

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement, as in 这, 近, 送: 过 is to pass or cross.
寸 here replaces 咼 (guō) of the traditional 過, so it is not a sound clue; 咼 survives in 锅 guō and 祸 huò.
广 (building) — 广 is a building radical, as in 店, 床; 度 also sounds out 渡 dù and 镀 dù.

example.hanzi: 医生提醒他不要过度饮酒。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng tíxǐng tā bùyào guòdù yǐnjiǔ.
example.english: The doctor reminded him not to drink excessively.
example.fact: The human liver can regenerate itself even after up to 70% of its tissue is removed or damaged, restoring most of its original mass within weeks. This remarkable capacity is also why liver transplants can come from living donors, who each regrow a functional liver from the portion they keep.

examples.hanzi: 过度疲劳会影响身体健康。
examples.pinyin: Guòdù píláo huì yǐngxiǎng shēntǐ jiànkāng.
examples.english: Excessive fatigue can harm your health.

examples.hanzi: 他对孩子的保护有点过度。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì háizi de bǎohù yǒudiǎn guòdù.
examples.english: He is a little overprotective of his child.
